doc.title: Louis Hayes interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000

title: Dexter Gordon's return and Live at the Vanguard
summary: The Louis Hayes-Woody Shaw group hosts Dexter Gordon's return to New York, with Maxine Gordon arranging it.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: The Dexter Gordon thing, you had that classic album with him too. That must have been a nice experience.
At the Vanguard. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -11-

Yes, yes. That was a great experience. That was with Woody. We had that group and Woody, excuse me I mean Dexter, was staying in Copenhagen at the time, and also Slide Hampton was living in Europe. So this lady Maxine, she talked to him about coming back to New York at the time, and Dexter wanted to do that. But he didn’t have a group. So when they put that together on, what was it Columbia? That album?

Columbia — Dexter made this into “Live at the Vanguard” and actually that was the Louis Hayes-Woody Shaw group but with Dexter. People were — it was such a big thing, for Dexter to come back. I mean the club was just packed every night, and it was such a warm feeling. It was a great experience. So we did some more things with Dexter at the time, but I’m glad I had that opportunity to make that history with Dexter at the time.
Yeah. He certainly had a persona to him.
The way he spoke and just his movements and all.
Exactly right. Dexter was one-of-a-kind, that’s for sure.
